extracted.intended_audience: educated readers of political essays, students of political philosophy, legislators and public intellectuals
extracted.subtask_description: Normative and stylistic guidance for political/philosophical writing and argumentation, and for the proper aims and limits of government in relation to religion and sectarian groups. Includes standards for fair public reasoning, treatment of minorities, and rhetorical clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign attachments are the fruit of domestic misrule
rubrics_metrics.description: If there be any proposition universally true in politics it is this, that foreign attachments are the fruit of domestic misrule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bigots make their subjects miserable at home and then complain they look for relief abroad; historical examples: Huguenots calling in England, Catholics calling in Spain, Protestants under Laud. Use this understanding to avoid blaming a sect's alleged 'foreignness' when it is produced by oppression and exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not infer conduct or loyalty from professed beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: It is altogether impossible to reason from the opinions which a man professes to his feelings and his actions; and in fact no person is ever such a fool as to reason thus, except when he wants a pretext for persecuting his neighbours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Calvinist doctrines do not imply immorality; Christians profess moral commands yet ordinary commercial behaviour does not assume full religious observance. Avoid using professed theology (e.g., predestination, eschatological hopes) as evidence of political disloyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers must create patriotism; they cannot absolve themselves of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the business of rulers to make [a sect] patriotic; the English Jews are precisely what our Government has made them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism that a group 'is not patriotic' is illegitimate when the government has treated them as aliens; to claim a class is unfit for political power after mistreatment is sophistry. Policy implication: remove oppressive restrictions and cultivate inclusion to foster civic attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confounding prophecy with precept is invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: We protest altogether against the practice of confounding prophecy with precept, of setting up predictions which are often obscure against a morality which is always clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use scriptural prophecies (e.g., predictions about the Jews' wanderings or restoration) to justify denying civil rights or to derive binding conduct rules. Distinguish predictive texts from moral injunctions when making public policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid persecutory sophistry based on remote or obscure doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: To charge men with practical consequences which they themselves deny is disingenuous in controversy; it is atrocious in government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: invoking papal bulls to label all Papists traitors; imputing to Jews actions they do not intend. Policy and rhetoric must not take remote doctrinal implications as proof of present danger or disloyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain division of labour: government's proper ends are temporal, not spiritual
rubrics_metrics.description: One great object is the protection of persons and property; another is the propagation of religious truth. No two objects more entirely distinct can well be imagined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: a pianoforte maker should not also be a baker. The state should secure life, property, and order, but is not by necessity the proper organ to promote or enforce a particular religion; combining unrelated institutional functions leads to poor results (e.g., bad arts and bad religious societies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject paternalistic government-as-parent overreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Gladstone conceives that the duties of governments are paternal; a doctrine which we shall not believe till he can show us some government which loves its subjects as a father loves a child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If government claims the moral role of selecting nurses, wives, hours of labor, reading, recreations, etc., it leads to absurd and oppressive control (Plato's full extent). Insist on limits to what governments may legitimately prescribe about private life and conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require solid foundations for doctrines with startling consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When the consequences of a doctrine are so startling, we may well require that its foundations shall be very solid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a political or constitutional doctrine would justify exclusion of groups, suppression of rights, or sweeping religious enforcement, demand very full and accurate demonstration (evidence and reasoning) before adopting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and rhetoric must not obscure logic; prefer clarity and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: His rhetoric, though often good of its kind, darkens and perplexes the logic which it should illustrate... That transparent haze... is more dangerous than utter darkness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political and philosophical writing should favor 'dry light'—precision and perspicuity—over 'dim magnificence' of lofty but vague diction. When propositions are to be demonstrated, avoid majestic language that disguises weak premises. Good style should illuminate, not delude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary oratorical skill does not substitute for philosophical depth
rubrics_metrics.description: The tendency of institutions like those of England is to encourage readiness in public men, at the expense both of fulness and of exactness... A politician must often talk and act before he has thought and read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the difference between debating talent and the ability to produce rigorous, original treatises; encourage deeper study and reflection in political authorship rather than relying on the artifices of oral eloquence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of remedial measures can be symbolically appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: We know of no day fitter for terminating long hostilities, and repairing cruel wrongs, than the day on which the religion of mercy was founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic timing (e.g., bringing a measure to relieve a persecuted group during Passion week) can be morally and rhetorically appropriate to emphasize reconciliation and the abolition of intolerance; do not reject reforms on spurious grounds of timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not generalize from nominal adherence to religious precepts to predict political behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The law which is inscribed on the walls of the synagogues prohibits covetousness. But if we were to say that a Jew mortgagee would not foreclose because God had commanded him not to covet his neighbour’s house, everybody would think us out of our wits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assuming that religious commandments will be followed strictly in ordinary economic and civic life; using such assumptions to predict political actions (or to deny rights) is ignorant of human nature and everyday practice.
